chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him),
regarding the words of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'And indeed it is a Reminder for you and for your people, and you shall soon be questioned' [43:44].
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Reminder (Al-Zikr) is the Quran, and we are its people, and we are the ones who will be questioned.'

key_terms.الذِّكْر: Al-Zikr — The Reminder, here interpreted as the Quran itself
key_terms.الْمَسْئُولُون: the ones to be questioned — those who bear responsibility and authority to be consulted
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted — an honorific epithet of God
key_terms.قَوْمُهُ: its people — the Ahl al-Bayt, the household of the Prophet (SAWW)

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'people of the Reminder' (Ahl al-Zikr) according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets Quran 43:44, where the Quran is described as 'a reminder for you and your people.' The Imam identifies the Ahl al-Bayt (his household) as the 'people of the Reminder' — those divinely designated to be the guardians, authoritative interpreters, and living references for the Quran. This teaching addresses the Shia theological position that the Imams are the Ahl al-Zikr (People of the Reminder) whom God commanded believers to consult regarding the Quran and religious matters (cf. Quran 16:43).

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High [43:44] And it is a Reminder for you and your people, and you shall soon be questioned.
Heasws said: ‘The Zikr (The Reminder) is the Quran, and weasws are its people, and weasws are the ones to be asked’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad from Rib‘iy from Fudayl form abu ’Abdallah (a.s.)
who has said the following about the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High. “It is a Dhikr for you and for your people and you all will be asked questions.’ [43:44]
The Imams (a.s.)said, “The Holy Quran is the ’Dhikr’ and we are the one who will be asked questions.”
